#Dogecoin's rise, to me, is a reminder to the world not to take things too seriously.

I don't know how people still do, given what happened over the last few years, but there's still plenty of people out there pretending. I'm glad humor still has a place on this world. Good dog!

$DOGE, like $BTC, is very simple thing. #Bitcoin is a store of value, #Dogecoin has been used as a semi-stable currency for tipping for years. Doesn't have all those fancy (potential) features #ADA claims it will have, but it doesn't have to pretend, that's why people love it.

The "#Dogecoin is going to bring in regulations" argument is ridiculous, especially given the fact that there's literally a case going on with #XRP and the SEC right now.

At the time, $ETH was the new kid on the block and wasn't taken seriously by the Bitcoin Maxis. (That's still true, I guess.) But ETH had a dream of making smart contracts https://t.co/2zIYdFR0xq

Why/How did #Dogecoin get so successful? The answer is surprisingly easy: Good Times. When $DOGE was a small puppy-dog run by a few people in San Francisco, they put on IRL meetup events regularly that were legendary - I still hear people talk about those days with fond memories.

Sent by a friend. I sold off all my $DOGE (the crypto, not the new thing) as soon as Elon started meddling with it but who knew how perverse the whole thing would become.
